Differentiate the units, integrate them, and omit the particular measurements

feedback.note: Differentiation, integration, and measurement-omission are one ordered process. The units are set apart by a shared characteristic, united into one mental entity, and the particular measurements are omitted. Starting from a stipulated word is subjectivism. Waiting for a form in the object is intrinsicism, because it denies the method.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about what a concept is?
exercises.quote: A concept is a mental integration of two or more units possessing the same distinguishing characteristic(s), with their particular measurements omitted.

choices.text: A concept integrates units that share a distinguishing characteristic, with the particular measurements omitted.
A concept is a form in the object, and the mind contributes no integration. No mind unites the units.
A concept is an arbitrary label, and the measurements are a matter of preference. Preference selects the measurements.
A concept keeps every particular measurement and drops the characteristic. Identical concretes alone can share it.

feedback.quote: A concept is a mental integration of two or more units possessing the same distinguishing characteristic(s), with their particular measurements omitted.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Concept-Formation," Introduction to Objectivist Epistemology, 13
feedback.note: The passage states one process: a mental integration of two or more units that share a distinguishing characteristic, with the particular measurements omitted. A form revealed with no work is intrinsicism, because it denies the method. An arbitrary label is subjectivism. Keeping the measurements and dropping the characteristic reverses the omission the passage names.

exercises.prompt: Walk "table" through the process. Which account completes every part?

choices.text: Notice one table, keep its exact height, and ignore every other table, the concept reduced to one concrete
Set tables apart from other furniture, unite them as one mental unit, and omit the particular sizes
Feel that some objects belong together, and skip any shared characteristic, mood replacing the shared trait
Find the concept already in the wood, then omit the need to look, the wood doing the integrating

feedback.note: Tables are differentiated from the wider background, integrated into one concept, and their particular measurements are omitted so that other sizes still count. Stopping at one table's height refuses the omission. A feeling with no characteristic is subjectivism. A form already in the wood is intrinsicism, because it cancels the method.

exercises.prompt: Match each view of concepts to the claim it makes.

pairs.right: A method based on facts: differentiate, integrate, omit measurements
The concept is revealed in the object, with no mental work
The concept is an arbitrary invention, not based on a shared fact
One unit's measurements are kept, so the concept never opens

feedback.note: Concepts are objective when they are formed by a method based on facts. Intrinsicism denies the work and treats the concept as revealed in the object. Subjectivism treats it as an arbitrary invention. A prototype rule is a further failure of omission, because the particular measurements were supposed to be left out.

exercises.prompt: Complete the three names of the one process, in order.

parts.text: The process is
, then integration, then measurement-omission.

feedback.note: The ordered process begins with differentiation, then integrates the units, then omits the particular measurements. Stipulation is subjectivism, because the word is chosen apart from the facts. Revelation is intrinsicism, a concept supposed to announce itself in the object. Neutrality is not a step in forming a concept at all.

exercises.prompt: A speaker omits sizes, colors, and uses all at once and calls the result a concept, with no shared characteristic. Which part of the process is missing?

choices.text: Nothing. Omission alone is enough, whatever the items are
A vote, which can supply the characteristic the items lack
Differentiation. Nothing was isolated by a distinguishing characteristic
A form in the objects, which should have made the mixture one essence

feedback.note: Omission applies to the measurements of a characteristic the units share. Without differentiation there is no such characteristic, and the "concept" is an arbitrary collection. That is subjectivism, because no shared fact was isolated. A vote cannot install a shared fact that is not there, and intrinsicism cannot find an essence in a mixture that was never set apart.

exercises.prompt: Someone differentiates and integrates the ropes, then treats 5 feet as essential to "rope." Which part did he undo?

choices.text: He undid perception, because ropes are not perceived, the ropes having been invisible
He undid differentiation, because length was never a characteristic, no contrast drawn
He undid nothing, because a concept should freeze one measurement, prototypes required
He undid measurement-omission, because other lengths of rope are then excluded

feedback.note: The ropes were properly set apart and united as one kind. Freezing one length puts a particular measurement back into the concept. Other ropes then fail to qualify for a difference the process was supposed to omit. The error is a failure of omission, because that length was supposed to stay open, not a discovery that concepts must be prototypes.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim that concepts are objective rather than revealed or invented.

feedback.note: A concept is objective because it is formed by a method based on facts: differentiation, integration, and measurement-omission. Revelation would be intrinsicism, a concept disclosed in the object with no work. An arbitrary invention would be subjectivism, a label with no distinguishing characteristic in the units.

exercises.prompt: When, in the order of concept-formation, does a definition come?

choices.text: After the units are integrated, as a statement of what kind they are
Before any units are noticed, as a stipulation that creates them
Instead of integration, so the sentence is the whole concept
Only after every fact in the world has been learned

feedback.note: The units are integrated first. The definition then states what kind they are. It is the last step, not the act that creates the concept. Starting from a stipulated sentence reverses the order. Treating the definition as the whole meaning leaves out the units, because the concept refers to the existents that were integrated.

exercises.prompt: A child uses "dog" correctly for the animals she has integrated, but cannot yet state a definition. Does she have the concept?

choices.text: No. A concept exists only when a definition has been written
Yes. The definition states the kind later. It does not create the integration
Yes, but only because a definition is a private sentence she may skip forever
No. Until the sentence exists, the animals are not perceived

feedback.note: She has integrated the units, so she has the concept. The definition is a later condensation of what distinguishes them. Requiring the sentence first reverses the order. Calling the definition a sentence she may skip forever is a different error, because a definition is still required when she is able to state the kind. It is not optional in principle and not prior in time.

exercises.prompt: A committee writes "a flarn is whatever we say it is" and then goes looking for examples. What has been reversed?

choices.text: Nothing. A definition is supposed to create the units
The percepts, which should have been adjusted to the sentence
The order. The units must be integrated before a definition states their kind
Measurement-omission, which belongs in the definition's opening words

feedback.note: A definition states the kind of units already integrated. Inventing the sentence first, with the units still unfound, is a private stipulation. That is subjectivism about meaning, because the word does not record a group set apart from the facts. It announces a decision and hunts for illustrations afterward.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the place it has relative to a definition.

pairs.right: Come first. The concept already refers to them
Comes after, and states what kind those units are
Reverses the order and records no group
Remain the meaning. The definition does not replace them

feedback.note: Integration comes before definition. The definition states the kind. It does not replace the units as the meaning of the concept. A stipulation with nothing integrated is not that last step, because there is no group whose kind is being stated. The error treats a sentence as if it could precede the facts.

exercises.prompt: Complete the order between the concept and its definition.

parts.text: The units are integrated first. The definition comes

feedback.note: The definition comes after the units are integrated. Putting it before reverses concept-formation into a stipulation. Putting it instead of the integration treats the sentence as the whole concept, which leaves out the units. Never stating a kind, once the knowledge is available, is a different failure, not a reason to place the sentence first.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the meaning of a concept is only the defining sentence, not the existents integrated under it. What has he dropped?

choices.text: The sentence. A concept should have no statement of kind at all, meaning lost
The percepts, which a definition is supposed to cancel, erasure being the point
Nothing. A concept is a sentence and the existents are optional, referents lost
The units. The definition condenses their kind. It does not replace them

feedback.note: The concept means the units it integrates. The definition states the distinguishing kind of those units. It is a condensation, not a substitute. The error reduces the concept to a form of words, because the existents then drop out of the meaning and the sentence is asked to do the work of the integration.

exercises.prompt: Which performance shows that a person has reached the last step, rather than stopped at integration?

choices.text: He states the kind of units he has already integrated
He points to the units and has no words for what sets them apart
He invents a sentence and has not yet found any units
He remembers each unit separately and never unites them

feedback.note: The last step states the kind of units already united. Pointing without a statement of kind may show the concept, but not yet the definition. A sentence with no units is a stipulation. Separate memories are not even the integration. The definition comes after that union, because it condenses a distinction already made.

exercises.prompt: Build the order that keeps the definition from pretending to create the concept.

feedback.note: The units are integrated first, and the definition then states their kind. Doing it before looking, or by stipulation, reverses the order. That error is subjectivism about the sentence, because a definition does not bring the units into existence. It identifies what kind the integrated units are.

exercises.prompt: What two parts does a proper definition state?

choices.text: A differentia only, with no wider group named, the mark floating with no class around it
A genus, the wider group, and a differentia, the characteristic that sets these units apart
A genus only, wide enough that nothing is set apart, the wider name being the whole definition
Every attribute the units happen to have, listed without selection, an inventory, not a definition

feedback.note: A definition states a genus and a differentia. The genus is the wider group. The differentia sets these units apart inside it. A differentia with no genus does not say what kind of wider group is being divided. A genus with no differentia does not distinguish. A full list of attributes is an inventory, not a definition.

exercises.prompt: In the definition "man is a rational animal," which word is the genus and which is the differentia?

choices.text: Rational is the genus, and animal is the differentia
Both words are differentiae, and no genus is stated
Animal is the genus, and rational is the differentia
Both words are private labels, with no wider group in the facts

feedback.note: Animal is the wider group, the genus. Rational is the characteristic that sets human beings apart within that group, the differentia. Reversing them makes rationality the wider class and animality the distinction, which does not match the units. Calling both words private labels is subjectivism, because the definition records a real division.

exercises.prompt: Someone defines a triangle only as "three-sided" and never says three-sided what. What is missing?

choices.text: A second differentia that repeats the first, repeated before any genus
A vote on whether sides are fashionable, fashion completing the definition
The omission of the fact that triangles have sides, the stated trait deleted
The genus, the wider group inside which the differentia distinguishes

feedback.note: Three-sided distinguishes triangles only inside a wider group, such as plane figures. Without the genus, the differentia is an incomplete definition. It does not say what kind of thing is being set apart. The error leaves out the genus, because a distinguishing characteristic distinguishes inside a wider class, not in a void.

exercises.prompt: Match each formula to the definitional fault or success it shows.

pairs.right: Genus and differentia both present
Differentia without a genus
Genus without a differentia

pairs.left: Man is whatever I stipulate today
pairs.right: A private formula, not a genus or a differentia

feedback.note: "Rational animal" states the wider group and the characteristic that sets men apart inside it. "Rational" alone omits the genus. "Animal" alone does not distinguish man from other animals. A stipulation is neither part, because a definition is not a private decision about how a word will be used today.

exercises.prompt: Complete the two parts of a definition, in the usual order.

parts.text: A definition states the
and the

feedback.note: The genus is the wider group, and the differentia is the characteristic that sets these units apart inside it. A feeling is not either part, because a definition states facts about the units, not an estimate. A vote does not become a differentia. Subjectivism would treat the parts as optional labels.

exercises.prompt: A reference page lists man as warm, feathered or not, tool-using, speaking, mortal, and two-legged, and calls the list the definition. What went wrong?

choices.text: An inventory of attributes is not a genus plus one distinguishing differentia
A definition should avoid saying what wider group the units belong to
The list fails only because it includes a true attribute
The list is fine if the longest list is what "fundamental" means

feedback.note: A definition selects the wider group and the characteristic that sets the units apart. It does not transcribe every attribute. The error confuses a definition with an inventory, because the distinguishing work is lost in the pile. Length is not fundamentality. The differentia is the characteristic that explains the others, not the one that makes the longest page.

exercises.prompt: Which repair turns "man is an animal" into a definition?

choices.text: Add a second genus and still name no distinction
Add the differentia that sets human beings apart within animals
Replace animal with a feeling about people
Stipulate that animal will mean whatever is convenient today

feedback.note: "Animal" is only the genus. The definition needs the differentia, the characteristic that sets men apart inside that group, which is rationality. A feeling or a stipulation does not supply it. Those are subjectivism, because they do not name a characteristic the units possess and the rest of the genus lacks.

exercises.prompt: Build the definition of man that keeps the wider group and the distinction.

feedback.note: Man is a rational animal: animal is the genus, and rational is the differentia. Featherless names a surface mark that does not explain the distinctive character of the units. Stipulated names no fact at all. The error in both substitutes is that neither is the characteristic that sets men apart inside the genus by explaining the rest.

exercises.prompt: Which characteristic belongs in the differentia?

choices.text: The oddest surface mark, chosen because it is rare, rarity standing in for explanation
The characteristic a speaker stipulates for private convenience, convenience defining them
The one that explains the greatest number of the other distinguishing characteristics
Any true attribute, even one the wider group shares as well, distinction failing

feedback.note: The fundamental differentia explains the greatest number of the other distinguishing characteristics. An odd surface mark can be real and still explain almost nothing. A stipulation is subjectivism. An attribute the whole genus shares does not distinguish, because a differentia has to set these units apart inside the genus.

exercises.prompt: Why is "rational" the differentia of man, rather than "featherless" or "walks upright"?

choices.text: Because a tradition voted the other marks out
Because surface marks are never perceived, so they cannot be mentioned
Because a differentia should be the attribute that is hardest to observe
Because rationality explains far more of man's distinctive characteristics

feedback.note: Rationality explains language, knowledge, technology, and the chosen form of human life. Walking upright and lacking feathers explain far less. They can be real surface marks and still fail as the differentia. The error is selecting the odd or obvious mark, because fundamentality is explanatory power, not rarity or ease of view.

exercises.prompt: Speech is distinctive of human beings. Why is "the speaking animal" still a weaker definition than "the rational animal," once reason is known?

choices.text: Speech is a consequence of rationality, so it explains less than the faculty that makes it possible
Speech is false, so it cannot be a human characteristic, a real consequence barred from mankind
Speech is fundamental because it is easier to hear than reason is to grasp, hearing outranking reason
Any consequence is automatically more fundamental than its cause, the effect explaining its cause

feedback.note: Speech distinguishes men, but it depends on the rational faculty. Once that is known, rationality explains speech and a wide range of other characteristics, while speech explains fewer of them. Choosing the consequence as the differentia stops short of the fundamental. The error prefers a recognizable result over the characteristic that explains it.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed differentia of man to the verdict it deserves.

pairs.right: Fundamental, because it explains the greatest number of the others
A surface mark that explains almost none of the others
Fails to distinguish, because the wider group shares it
A stipulation, not a characteristic of the units

feedback.note: The fundamental differentia is the characteristic that explains the most of the others. Featherless is an odd surface mark, not that explanation. Having a heart does not set men apart inside animals. A preference is subjectivism, because a differentia has to be a fact about the units, not a private decision about the word.

exercises.prompt: Complete the test for the characteristic that belongs in the differentia.

parts.text: Choose the characteristic that explains the greatest number of the

feedback.note: The fundamental characteristic explains the greatest number of the other distinguishing characteristics. The oddest exception is a surface mark, not that explanation. Feelings and votes do not rank characteristics, because fundamentality is an objective relation among the facts, not a preference about which mark is most striking.

exercises.prompt: Someone says the essence is a ghostly ingredient he intuits in the object, so he need not ask which characteristic explains the others. Which view is that?

choices.text: The rule that the differentia must explain the greatest number of the others
Intrinsicism: the essence is revealed, with no method of selection
A genus-and-differentia definition stated after the units are known
Measurement-omission inside concept-formation

feedback.note: Selecting the fundamental characteristic is a method: find the one that explains the most of the others. Intrinsicism replaces that work with an essence supposed to announce itself in the object. The error denies the need to rank characteristics, because nothing is fundamental merely by being felt as an inner core.

exercises.prompt: A mark is easy to see, true of the units, and explains none of their other distinctive features. What should be done with it?

choices.text: Make it the differentia, because ease of observation is fundamentality, the shallow mark defining it
Deny the mark, because only invisible traits are allowed in a definition, true marks struck out
Keep it as a fact, but do not use it as the differentia once a deeper characteristic is known
Stipulate it as the meaning, since the word is ours to assign, assignment replacing explanation

feedback.note: An obvious mark can be real without being fundamental. It stays a fact about the units. It does not become the differentia if another characteristic explains more of the rest. The error equates "easiest to see" with "explains the most." A stipulation would abandon the facts altogether rather than rank them.

exercises.prompt: Build the test that selects a differentia without using rarity as a shortcut.

feedback.note: The fundamental characteristic explains the greatest number of the others. The oddest surface mark can distinguish in a thin way and still explain nothing further. Choosing it mistakes rarity for fundamentality. A definition needs the characteristic on which the greatest number of the remaining distinctions depend.

exercises.prompt: How are concepts ordered relative to one another?

choices.text: In a pile: every concept is read directly off percepts at the same level, side by side
By stipulation: each word is independent of every other word, each word a separate base
By feeling: the most vivid word is the base, whatever it refers to, intensity as order
In a hierarchy: later concepts rest on earlier ones, not in a flat pile of labels

feedback.note: Concepts form a hierarchy. First-level concepts are formed from percepts, and later concepts are formed from earlier concepts. A flat pile treats "furniture" as if it were perceived alongside tables, with no dependence. That error leaves out the order, because a wider concept cannot be formed before the units it integrates are known.

exercises.prompt: What has to be grasped before the concept "furniture" can be formed?

choices.text: Earlier concepts such as table, chair, and bed, themselves drawn from percepts
Only the word furniture, with no grasp of tables, chairs, or beds
A single percept of furniture that is not a percept of any particular thing
A vote that creates furniture without reference to any objects

feedback.note: Furniture is a higher-level concept. It integrates earlier concepts such as table, chair, and bed, and those were formed from percepts. There is no percept of furniture apart from such things. Treating the wider word as a first-level label ignores the hierarchy, because the later concept rests on the earlier ones.

exercises.prompt: A student tries to learn "organism" while refusing to learn any particular kind of living thing. Where does that break the order?

choices.text: Nowhere. Wider concepts are perceived directly and need no earlier concepts
The wider concept rests on earlier concepts of living things, which he has refused
It breaks perception, because organisms cannot be observed at all
It breaks only the spelling of the word, not its dependence

feedback.note: "Organism" integrates earlier concepts of plants, animals, and other living things. Those earlier concepts rest in turn on percepts. Refusing them and keeping the wide word treats a later concept as if it came first. The error inverts the hierarchy, because there is nothing for the wider integration to unite.

exercises.prompt: Match each concept to the level it occupies.

pairs.right: A concrete given in perception, not yet a concept
A first-level concept, formed from percepts
A wider concept that rests on earlier concepts such as table and chair

pairs.left: A label in a flat list
pairs.right: A denial of the dependence later concepts have on earlier ones

feedback.note: A single table is perceived. The concept "table" integrates perceived tables. "Furniture" integrates earlier concepts and cannot be formed from a special percept of its own. Calling every word a label at one level denies that order. The error treats a hierarchy as a pile, because dependence is part of what the later concept is.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast between an order of concepts and a heap of words.

parts.text: Concepts form a hierarchy, not a

feedback.note: A hierarchy means later concepts rest on earlier ones. A pile would make every concept a direct label on percepts, with no dependence. A percept is not the thing being rejected. The genus is part of a definition, not the name of the false picture. The error in the pile is that it leaves out the order.

exercises.prompt: Someone uses the concept "science" to argue that first-level concepts from percepts are impossible. What has the dependence been asked to do?

choices.text: A first-level concept has been formed from percepts in the ordinary way
A wider concept has been reduced to the earlier concepts that support it
A later concept has been used to cancel the earlier knowledge it rests on
A definition has stated a genus and a differentia

feedback.note: Science rests on earlier concepts, which rest on percepts. Using science to deny that base asks a later item to destroy what makes it possible. The error inverts the hierarchy, because the later concept has no content without that base. Reducing a wider concept to its earlier base is the opposite, and legitimate, move. It keeps the order instead of cancelling it.

exercises.prompt: Which statement confuses "abstract" with "baseless"?

choices.text: Furniture rests on table, chair, and bed
Table is formed from perceived tables
A later concept may not be used to deny the earlier concepts it needs
Any concept wider than a percept is a flat label with no base

feedback.note: Width is not baselessness. A wider concept has a base if it rests on earlier concepts and, through them, on percepts. Calling every abstraction a flat label confuses the hierarchy with a pile of empty words. The error leaves out the order of dependence, because abstract and floating are not the same charge.

exercises.prompt: Build the rule that keeps a wider concept from pretending to come first.

feedback.note: Later concepts rest on earlier ones and cannot replace that base. Floating free of the earlier concepts would turn the wider word into a label with nothing integrated. Cancelling the earlier concepts while keeping the later one inverts the hierarchy, because the wider concept has no content except what the earlier ones provide.

exercises.prompt: What does it mean that a definition is contextual?

choices.text: It states the fundamentals in the order of one's present knowledge, and can be restated when that knowledge deepens
It is a private stipulation that may change whenever the word feels different, and the units may be dropped with the mood
It drops the original units as soon as a deeper characteristic is known, the old referents discarded
It is fixed to the first surface mark, and deeper knowledge is irrelevant, restatement being forbidden

feedback.note: A definition states the fundamental characteristic available in one's knowledge. When knowledge deepens, the differentia can be restated to a characteristic that explains more. The units stay. A stipulation that changes by mood is subjectivism, because context is not a license to reassign the word. Clinging to the first surface mark refuses the restatement. Dropping the units abandons the concept.

exercises.prompt: People were first set apart as "the animals that walk upright." Deeper knowledge shows that rationality explains far more. What is the right restatement?

choices.text: Drop the human beings and attach the word man to a new, empty class
Restate the differentia as rational, and keep the same human beings as the units
Keep "walks upright" forever, because the first mark is beyond correction
Let each speaker stipulate a private differentia for the same word

feedback.note: Walking upright was a less fundamental mark of the same units. Rationality explains more of what distinguishes them, so the definition is restated and the human beings remain. Dropping the units would replace the concept. Freezing the surface mark refuses a deeper fundamentality. A private differentia is subjectivism, because the restatement has to track the facts.

exercises.prompt: Water was identified by observed properties, and later knowledge states its chemical composition. Which outcome keeps the concept?

choices.text: The observed water is dismissed as having referred to nothing
The word is reassigned by vote to a liquid no one had integrated
The definition is restated, and the same substance remains the referent
The composition is declared unknowable, so the first surface list is frozen

feedback.note: Contextual restatement keeps the units. The water that was perceived is still what the concept refers to when the differentia is deepened. Saying the old concept referred to nothing drops the units. Reassigning the word by vote is subjectivism. Freezing the surface list treats the first context of knowledge as if it could not be deepened.

exercises.prompt: Match each response to what it does when knowledge of the units deepens.

pairs.left: Restate the differentia and keep the units
pairs.right: A contextual definition, updated without abandoning the referents

pairs.left: Keep the first surface mark forever
pairs.right: A refusal to let a more fundamental characteristic take its place

pairs.left: Drop the units and keep the word
pairs.right: A break in the concept, not a restatement of it
A stipulation, not a definition ordered by knowledge

feedback.note: A contextual definition states the fundamentals in the order of one's knowledge. Deeper knowledge can restate the differentia without dropping the units. Freezing the surface mark ignores that order. Dropping the units, or changing the word by mood, does not restate fundamentality. Those errors replace the concept or treat it as subjectivism.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rule that keeps the referents when a definition is restated.

parts.text: Restate the fundamentality without dropping the

feedback.note: The units stay. What changes, when knowledge deepens, is the statement of which characteristic is fundamental. Keeping only the word, while dropping the units, is not a contextual restatement. A mood or a vote would make the new sentence a stipulation, because the referents would no longer control the definition.

exercises.prompt: Someone says "definitions are contextual" and concludes he may mean anything he likes by the word today. What did he trade the rule for?

choices.text: A restatement that keeps the same units under a deeper differentia, as if a mood were that restatement
A genus and a differentia stated after the units are integrated, as if a whim were genus and differentia
The omission of particular measurements inside a stable concept, as if a whim were measurement-omission
A private stipulation. Context here means the order of knowledge, not a license to reassign the word

feedback.note: Contextual names the dependence of the definition on one's knowledge of the units. It does not mean the meaning is a preference. The error is subjectivism, a stipulation dressed up as context. A genuine restatement keeps the units and only changes which characteristic is cited as fundamental.

exercises.prompt: Deeper knowledge shows a new characteristic that explains more, but it belongs to a different set of existents. What would it be wrong to do?

choices.text: Hand the original word to the new set and declare the old units dropped
Leave the original concept with its own units and form a new concept for the new set
Ask whether the new characteristic is fundamental for the original units
Keep the original units if the new characteristic is in fact theirs

feedback.note: A restatement deepens the differentia of the same units. If the new characteristic picks out other existents, those are not a restatement of this concept. They may deserve a concept of their own. Dropping the original units and reassigning the word breaks the concept. The error treats added knowledge as a license to abandon the referents.

exercises.prompt: Build the rule that deepens a definition without abandoning what it was about.

feedback.note: Later knowledge can restate which characteristic is fundamental, and the units remain. Dropping them would turn the new sentence into a different concept wearing the old word. A private stipulation would change the meaning, because no deeper knowledge of the units would justify it. Context is the order of knowledge about the same units, not a license to discard them.

exercises.prompt: What is objectivity, as a policy toward the facts?

choices.text: Neutrality that gives a fact and a contradiction equal weight
Volitional adherence to reality by the method of logic
A vote that decides which facts the group will recognize
A mind that writes the facts to match a preference

feedback.note: Objectivity is a chosen adherence to reality, carried out by the method of logic. Neutrality treats evidence and error as equal claimants, which abandons adherence. A vote is subjectivism about the facts. A mind that writes reality reverses the order, because consciousness has to conform to what exists, not the other way around.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about the status of facts?
exercises.quote: Reality exists as an objective absolute—facts are facts, independent of man's feelings, wishes, hopes or fears.

choices.text: Facts become real when a feeling or a wish brings them into line.
Objectivity means staying neutral between a fact and a wish.
Facts are independent of feelings, wishes, hopes, and fears.
A vote is what makes a fact independent of the voters.

feedback.quote: Reality exists as an objective absolute—facts are facts, independent of man's feelings, wishes, hopes or fears.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "Introducing Objectivism," The Objectivist Newsletter, August 1962, 35
feedback.note: The passage says reality is an objective absolute: facts are independent of feelings, wishes, hopes, and fears. Objectivity adheres to that independence. It does not create it. Neutrality between a fact and a wish is not what the passage establishes, because a wish has no power to stand beside a fact as an equal source.

exercises.prompt: A panel is asked to be objective about a cracked beam. They split the credit equally between the crack and a hope that the beam is sound. What did they substitute for objectivity?

choices.text: Adherence to the crack by identifying what the beam is, hope excluded
Logic, understood as non-contradictory identification, on the crack
A restatement of the evidence without dropping the beam, crack retained
Neutrality, which treats a hope as the equal of a perceived fact

feedback.note: The crack is a fact. The hope is not a second fact of the same kind. Splitting the credit is neutrality, a refusal to adhere. The error pretends that fairness to a wish is objectivity, because it gives a non-cognitive claim the status of evidence. Adherence would identify the beam as cracked.

exercises.prompt: Match each policy to the relation it actually has to the facts.

pairs.right: Chosen adherence to reality by the method of logic
A refusal to let the evidence outweigh a contradiction or a wish
An attempt to make agreement the author of the facts
Subjectivism: consciousness is treated as the source of the facts

feedback.note: Objectivity adheres to facts that are independent of feelings and wishes. Neutrality will not adhere. A vote and a mind that writes the facts are both subjectivism, because they treat consciousness as if it could decide what exists. The facts do not wait on that decision.

exercises.prompt: Complete the name of the policy that follows the facts on purpose.

parts.text: Objectivity is volitional adherence to

feedback.note: Objectivity is volitional adherence to reality, by the method of logic. Neutrality, opinion, and feeling are the substitutes people offer when they will not adhere. Those substitutes fail because none of them is a method of identifying facts that exist independent of the identifier.

exercises.prompt: Someone says he is objective because he lets his conclusions rewrite the measurements that conflict with them. Which error is that?

choices.text: Subjectivism: the mind is treated as the author of the facts
Adherence: the measurements are kept and the conclusion is checked against them
Logic: a contradiction is used as a sign that the conclusion failed
Context: the conclusion is held inside the evidence that supports it

feedback.note: Rewriting the measurements to save a conclusion makes consciousness the author of the facts. That is subjectivism, the opposite of adherence. Objectivity would keep the measurements and change the conclusion, because the facts do not conform to the mind. A contradiction is a signal to correct the thinking, not a license to edit reality.

exercises.prompt: A researcher has conclusive evidence and still calls a refusal to judge "objectivity." What has the word been emptied of?

choices.text: Nothing. Objectivity means withholding judgment no matter what the evidence is
Adherence. Objectivity is the choice to judge by the facts, not the choice to abstain
The vote, which should have replaced the evidence
The wish, which should have been given equal standing with the result

feedback.note: When the evidence warrants a conclusion, objectivity concludes. Abstaining in the name of objectivity is neutrality wearing a stolen word. The error empties adherence out of the concept, because a method of knowing the facts is precisely a method of judging them, not a pose of having no answer.

exercises.prompt: Build the statement of objectivity that rules out neutrality and invention.

feedback.note: Objectivity is volitional adherence to reality by the method of logic. Neutrality would refuse to let the facts decide. A mind that writes reality would be subjectivism, because the facts would then depend on the consciousness that was supposed to know them. Adherence keeps the direction: the mind conforms to existence.

exercises.prompt: What method does objectivity use in adhering to the facts?

choices.text: Whatever works for the moment, whether or not it identifies the facts
A feeling of clarity, taken as proof that the conclusion is true
Logic, the art of non-contradictory identification
Verbal consistency among words that identify nothing

feedback.note: The method of objectivity is logic: non-contradictory identification of the facts. Pragmatism substitutes what works. A feeling of clarity is not identification, because emotion is not a tool of cognition. Words that never identify anything can be verbally tidy and still fail, since logic is identification, not a game of symbols.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about the nature of logic?
exercises.quote: Logic is the art of non-contradictory identification.

choices.text: Logic is a word game that need not identify any fact.
Logic is a contradiction maintained because it feels profound.
Logic is whatever result happens to work this week.
Logic is the art of identifying without contradiction.

feedback.quote: Logic is the art of non-contradictory identification.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125
feedback.note: The passage names two requirements together: identification, and non-contradiction. A word game drops the identification. A cherished contradiction drops the other half. What works is pragmatism, not this definition, because success is not a substitute for identifying what is, free of contradiction.

exercises.prompt: An accountant's books balance, and every figure was copied from a wish list rather than from the warehouse. Has he practiced logic?

choices.text: No. The figures contradict nothing and identify nothing in the warehouse
Yes. Non-contradiction among sentences is the whole of logic, wish list included
Yes. The books work as a story, so they are an identification, by being tidy
No. Logic forbids arithmetic even when the count is real, real counts forbidden

feedback.note: The books are verbally consistent and cognitively empty. Logic is non-contradictory identification, so both halves are required. Consistency with a wish list is not identification of the warehouse. The error reduces logic to a symbol game, because no fact has been identified. Pragmatism would add the further mistake of calling the story true because it is tidy.

exercises.prompt: Match each practice to the standard it actually uses.

pairs.right: The method of objectivity
Pragmatism, a substitute for identifying what is
Emotion used as a pretended tool of cognition
A symbol game that never reaches the facts

feedback.note: Objectivity adheres by logic, and logic identifies the facts without contradiction. What works replaces that standard with pragmatism. A feeling replaces it with mysticism, because emotion does not discover facts. Consistent words that identify nothing keep only half of logic and drop the identification.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of the method objectivity requires.

parts.text: Logic is the art of non-contradictory

feedback.quote: Logic is the art of non-contradictory identification.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 125
feedback.note: Logic is the art of non-contradictory identification. Invention would make the mind the author of the facts, which is subjectivism. Neutrality refuses to identify. Feeling is not a method of cognition, because what one feels reports an estimate rather than a fact. The method has to identify what exists.

exercises.prompt: A conclusion follows from an arbitrary premise and contradicts no sentence inside that story. Why is it still not the method of objectivity?

choices.text: Objectivity accepts any consistent story, since facts are optional, fiction included
Nothing in reality has been identified. Consistency with an empty premise is not logic
A contradiction with the warehouse would be a better method, clashing preferred to naming
The premise is objective precisely because no evidence ties it to anything, by being empty

feedback.note: Logic identifies what is. A conclusion that only avoids clashing with an arbitrary premise has identified nothing. The error treats non-contradiction as a game played inside a fiction, because the other half of the art, identification, is missing. An empty premise does not become objective by being isolated from the facts.

exercises.prompt: Two reports of one tank cannot both be right: it cannot be entirely full and entirely empty at once. Which response is logic?

choices.text: Keep both reports, because a contradiction shows depth, full and empty together
Average the two reports and call the average what works, a midpoint replacing the level
Treat the clash as a sign that an identification has failed, and find which one
Let a feeling decide which report is kinder, comfort choosing and the clash kept

feedback.note: Non-contradictory identification cannot leave the tank entirely full and entirely empty in the same respect at the same time. The clash confesses an error in one of the reports or in the inference. Keeping both, or letting a feeling choose, abandons the method. Averaging them is pragmatism, because it does not identify the tank.

exercises.prompt: Build the method that objectivity actually uses.

feedback.note: The method is non-contradictory identification of the facts. Invention of a wish would reverse adherence, because the mind would be writing what it was obliged to know. Logic is an art practiced on reality. It is not a way of making reality match a preference.

exercises.prompt: What is given in awareness, and what still has to be chosen?

choices.text: Percepts are chosen, and the facts rewrite themselves to match
Both the facts and the focus are automatic, so evasion is impossible
Nothing is given. Every content of awareness is a stipulation
Percepts are given. Adherence to them by logic is a choice

feedback.note: At the perceptual level, awareness is not chosen. The organs deliver percepts with no volition to invent them. The choice is to focus and to adhere to that given by logic. Determinism denies the choice. Subjectivism denies the given, because it treats the percept as something the person decided into existence.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about where volition enters cognition?
exercises.quote: The pre-conceptual level of consciousness is nonvolitional; volition begins with the first syllogism.

choices.text: The pre-conceptual level is not chosen. Volition begins with conceptual inference.
Percepts are chosen, and inference is automatic. Choice edits the given first.
Neither perception nor thought is chosen, so adherence is a myth. Evasion cannot occur.
Volition begins by rewriting the percepts the senses delivered. Before thought begins.

feedback.quote: The pre-conceptual level of consciousness is nonvolitional; volition begins with the first syllogism.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "For the New Intellectual," For the New Intellectual, 14
feedback.note: The passage draws the line at the first syllogism. Before that, consciousness is nonvolitional, so percepts are not inventions. Volition begins when thinking begins. The error of moving choice down into the percept is subjectivism. The error of denying choice at the conceptual level is determinism, because adherence would then be neither possible nor required.

exercises.prompt: A student sees the reading on the gauge and then decides whether to think about what it means. Which part was chosen?

choices.text: The reading itself, which his preference wrote onto the gauge
The choice to focus and identify the reading. The percept was given
Nothing. Seeing and thinking are the same automatic event
The laws of the gauge, which he can suspend by not focusing

feedback.note: The percept of the gauge is given. It is not a product of his decision. What he chooses is whether to focus and identify it by logic. That is adherence, and it is volitional. Treating the reading as written by his preference is subjectivism, because the pre-conceptual level has no volition with which to invent the gauge.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to the side of the line it falls on.

pairs.right: Given. The pre-conceptual level is nonvolitional
Volitional. One can think or drift
A further choice, not a stamp the percept applies by itself

pairs.left: A wish that alters the gauge
pairs.right: Not a power anyone has. The given does not obey it

feedback.note: Percepts are given because the pre-conceptual level is nonvolitional. Focusing, and then adhering by logic, are choices. A wish does not cross the line and edit the gauge. That error is subjectivism about the given. Determinism would make the opposite mistake and deny that focus is chosen at all.

exercises.prompt: Complete the line between what is given and what is chosen.

parts.text: The pre-conceptual level is

feedback.quote: The pre-conceptual level of consciousness is nonvolitional; volition begins with the first syllogism.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, "For the New Intellectual," For the New Intellectual, 14
feedback.note: The pre-conceptual level is nonvolitional, so percepts are not chosen and not invented. Calling that level optional would make the given a matter of taste, which is subjectivism, because the percept would then depend on a preference. Calling it mythical would deny awareness. Volition begins with thinking.

exercises.prompt: Someone says that because perception is automatic, every conclusion drawn from it is automatic too. What has he erased?

choices.text: The percept. Automatic awareness is a form of stipulation, the entity having been optional
Nothing. Objectivity is the name for a process no one can refuse, evasion identical with adherence
The choice to adhere. Conceptual identification is volitional even though the percept is not
Logic, which should be replaced by the feeling that follows a percept, emotion taking over

feedback.note: The percept is not chosen. The work of identifying it, without contradiction, is chosen. Determinism erases that choice and with it the difference between adherence and evasion. The error treats a nonvolitional given as if it carried the method of logic along for free, which it does not, because volition begins with conceptual thought.

exercises.prompt: A person chooses to focus, then claims the choice lets him decide what the gauge will say. What did he slide from?

choices.text: From evasion to a still more consistent evasion
From a given percept to a careful identification of it
From subjectivism to adherence, by picking the fact he prefers
From the choice to think to a pretended choice of the facts

feedback.note: The choice to focus is real, and it is not a choice of what the gauge reads. Sliding from one to the other is subjectivism, because the given remains whatever it is while he thinks or drifts. Adherence uses the choice to identify the reading. It does not use the choice to write the reading.

exercises.prompt: Build the line that keeps the given and the choice on their own sides.

feedback.note: Percepts are given, and adherence is chosen. Calling percepts invented is subjectivism, a mind writing the given. Calling adherence automatic is determinism, which denies the choice to focus and to follow logic. The two sides stay distinct because the pre-conceptual level is nonvolitional and conceptual thought is not.

exercises.prompt: In what setting does a conclusion hold, when objectivity is practiced?

choices.text: In the context of the evidence that supports it, not outside those facts
In every context at once, including the ones never investigated
In whatever story makes the conclusion convenient
In no context, because a conclusion may ignore the facts that gave it meaning

feedback.note: A conclusion holds in the context of the evidence that supports it. Using it while ignoring those facts is context-dropping, a failure of objectivity. Stretching it to every uninvestigated case claims more than the evidence. A convenient story is subjectivism, because context means the relevant facts, not a narrative chosen to protect the conclusion.

exercises.prompt: Tests show a solvent removes grease from metal at room temperature. An ad says the solvent "dissolves anything." What is the failure?

choices.text: Adherence to the tests, which named grease, metal, and temperature
Context-dropping: the conclusion is used while the limiting facts are ignored
A legitimate restatement that keeps the same units and the same limits
A percept of the solvent, which was never evidence

feedback.note: The conclusion was about grease on metal at room temperature. "Dissolves anything" keeps the triumphant word and drops the facts that gave it meaning. That is context-dropping, and it is a failure of objectivity, because adherence includes the evidence-context. It does not license a slogan cut off from the tests.

exercises.prompt: The advertiser replies that "in the context of the sale" the wider claim is true. What has "context" been turned into?

choices.text: The body of facts the tests actually established
A warning that the conclusion does not hold for untested materials
A story told to protect a conclusion the evidence will not support
The order in which later knowledge rests on earlier knowledge

feedback.note: A real context is the evidence a conclusion depends on. "The context of the sale" adds no fact about the solvent. It is a story. The error is subjectivism, because it uses the word context to mean a framing that preserves a wish. Objectivity would return the claim to grease, metal, and temperature.

exercises.prompt: Match each use of a conclusion to the cognitive act it is.

pairs.left: Holding the solvent claim inside the tests
pairs.right: Objectivity: the conclusion stays in its evidence
Context-dropping: the limits that gave the claim meaning are ignored

pairs.left: Inventing a sales story called a context
pairs.right: Subjectivism about what a context is

pairs.left: New tests on glass, kept distinct
pairs.right: A new context of evidence, not a rewrite of the old one

feedback.note: Objectivity holds a conclusion in the context of its evidence. Dropping grease, metal, and temperature while keeping the slogan is context-dropping. A sales story is not a new context of facts, because no evidence has been added. Further tests on glass would be a new context, and they would have to be identified on their own.

exercises.prompt: Complete the name of the failure that uses a conclusion and ignores its evidence.

parts.text: Using a conclusion while ignoring the facts that give it meaning is

feedback.note: Context-dropping uses an idea while ignoring the facts that give it meaning. That is a failure of objectivity, because adherence is to the evidence, not to a slogan cut free of it. Adherence is the policy that refuses this move. Integration and perception are earlier acts, not names for the failure.

exercises.prompt: A doctor says the drug helps condition C at dose D. A colleague cites "the drug works" as a reason to skip dose and condition. Which duty of objectivity did he drop?

choices.text: The duty to let a hopeful outcome enlarge the evidence
The duty to treat every untested illness as already included
The duty to remain neutral between the dose and a guess
The duty to keep the conclusion inside the evidence that supports it

feedback.note: The evidence supports a claim about condition C at dose D. Exporting "it works" past those facts drops the context. Objectivity forbids that, because a conclusion does not hold outside the evidence that supports it. Hope, an untested illness, and neutrality do not add the missing evidence. They abandon adherence.

exercises.prompt: Holding a conclusion in its context is not a claim to know every fact outside that context. Which temptation does that warning block?

choices.text: The temptation to treat a contextual conclusion as omniscience, or else as no conclusion
The temptation to name the evidence before using the conclusion, called the forbidden slide
The temptation to distinguish a new test from an old slogan, called the blocked temptation
The temptation to drop a limit because the slogan is shorter, called the threatened slide

feedback.note: A conclusion can be solid inside its evidence without being a claim about every fact beyond it. Stretching it is context-dropping, because the claim then outruns its evidence. Treating unknown facts elsewhere as if they emptied the known context is skepticism. Objectivity keeps that boundary.

exercises.prompt: Build the rule that keeps a conclusion tied to its evidence.

feedback.note: A conclusion holds in the context of its evidence. Any story would be subjectivism, a framing chosen to protect the words. Without its limits, the conclusion has been context-dropped. Objectivity fails in both substitutes, because adherence includes the facts that give the conclusion its meaning.

exercises.prompt: What does it mean that knowledge is hierarchical?

choices.text: Later conclusions are free to rewrite the earlier evidence, dependents rewriting the base
Later conclusions rest on earlier ones and cannot replace the base they depend on
Every conclusion is on one level and may cancel any other, one flat cancelling level
The latest theory is the base, and percepts are optional illustrations, mere ornament

feedback.note: Knowledge is hierarchical because later conclusions rest on earlier ones, down to percepts and the validity of the senses. A later conclusion cannot replace that base. A flat pile, or a theory that cancels the percepts it needed, inverts the order. The error pretends a dependent conclusion can stand first.

exercises.prompt: A bridge calculation rests on measurements, which rest on percepts. Someone cites the calculation to prove that measurement is impossible. What has he inverted?

choices.text: Nothing. A calculation may cancel the measurements it used
The arithmetic, which should have been replaced by a feeling about bridges
The order. A later conclusion has been used against the base it rests on
The percepts, which were never part of knowledge

feedback.note: The calculation has no standing except through the measurements, and the measurements have none except through percepts. Using the result to deny measurement replaces the base with a dependent conclusion. That violates the hierarchy of knowledge, because a later item cannot destroy the earlier items that give it content.

exercises.prompt: Which repair respects the hierarchy in that bridge case?

choices.text: Keep the calculation and discard the measurements as naive, the figure outranking the percepts it used
Keep the word bridge and drop every percept as optional, the name surviving its cancelled evidence
Let a vote decide whether measurement was real, the count replacing the measurement of the span
Trace the calculation back to the measurements and the percepts, and correct it there if it clashes

feedback.note: If the calculation clashes with a measurement, the error is in the later step or in a misread earlier step. The repair traces the dependence and corrects the identification. Discarding the measurements to save the result inverts the order. A vote is subjectivism, because it does not restore the base the conclusion rests on.

exercises.prompt: Match each move to what it does to an order of knowledge.

pairs.left: A theorem that uses its axioms
pairs.right: A later conclusion resting on earlier ones

pairs.left: A theorem used to deny its axioms
pairs.right: An inversion: the dependent item attacks its base
A denial that any conclusion rests on an earlier one

pairs.left: A correction traced to the first false step
pairs.right: Hierarchy respected: the base is kept and the error is found

feedback.note: Hierarchical knowledge means later conclusions rest on earlier ones and cannot replace them. Denying the axioms while keeping the theorem inverts that order. A flat pile denies the dependence altogether. Tracing a clash to the first false step is objectivity, because it uses the hierarchy instead of pretending the latest sentence is the base.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rule of order inside knowledge.

parts.text: Later conclusions rest on earlier ones and cannot replace the

feedback.note: Later conclusions rest on earlier ones and cannot replace the base they depend on. A wish, a vote, or a slogan is not that base. Substituting one of them is subjectivism or context-dropping, because the content of the later conclusion comes from the earlier knowledge, which has to stay in place.

exercises.prompt: Why is "science shows that we cannot know reality" a hierarchical failure, and not a modest conclusion?

choices.text: Science is later knowledge. It rests on knowing reality and cannot be used to deny that base
Science is the base, and percepts are a decorative extra, observation cancelled by the theory
Modesty requires every later conclusion to cancel the evidence it used, caution cancelling the base
The sentence is sound because a contradiction in the base is a scientific result, error promoted

feedback.note: Science depends on concepts, which depend on percepts, which are contact with reality. The sentence uses that structure to deny it. The failure is hierarchical, not a piece of caution, because a later conclusion cannot replace the base it rests on. Calling the contradiction a result mistakes an error in thinking for a discovery about knowledge.

exercises.prompt: A later experiment conflicts with an earlier measurement. Which response both keeps the hierarchy and practices objectivity?

choices.text: Throw out perception, since a later result outranks it, the percept discarded with the clash
Recheck both against the facts, without letting either cancel the nature of evidence
Throw out the experiment, since earlier items may never be rechecked, new evidence ignored
Keep both by saying each is true in its own story, two realities for one clash

feedback.note: A clash is a sign that some identification failed. Objectivity rechecks the experiment and the measurement. It does not let the later item abolish the perceptual base, and it does not freeze the earlier item against new evidence. Two stories would be subjectivism. The hierarchy says the later rests on the earlier. It does not say the earlier is immune to correction of an error.

exercises.prompt: Build the hierarchical rule that blocks a dependent conclusion from erasing its base.

feedback.note: Later conclusions rest on earlier ones and cannot replace that base. Letting them rewrite the base, or treating them as if they came before the evidence, inverts the hierarchy. Objectivity forbids the inversion, because a conclusion has meaning only through the earlier knowledge it depends on.

exercises.prompt: What is the only means of knowledge, and the only standard of truth?

choices.text: Emotion, when the feeling is strong enough to count as proof
Faith, a means that bypasses sensory evidence
Reason, the faculty that identifies and integrates sensory material
Whatever works, whether or not it identifies the facts

feedback.note: Reason is the only means of knowledge and the only standard of truth. It identifies and integrates the material the senses provide. Emotion used as proof is mysticism, and so is faith, because both claim a route around the evidence. What works is pragmatism, a substitute standard rather than the recognition of reality.

exercises.prompt: What does this passage establish about truth and the standard that judges it?
exercises.quote: Truth is the recognition of reality; reason, man's only means of knowledge, is his only standard of truth.

choices.text: Truth is a feeling of recognition, and emotion is the standard. A mood decides.
Truth is whatever works, and practical success is the standard. Useful errors qualify.
Truth is what a majority recognizes, and the count is the standard. The vote decides.
Truth is the recognition of reality, and reason is the only standard of truth.

feedback.quote: Truth is the recognition of reality; reason, man's only means of knowledge, is his only standard of truth.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 126
feedback.note: The passage ties truth to reality and names reason as the only means of knowledge and the only standard of truth. A feeling would make emotion the standard, which is mysticism. Success would make pragmatism the standard. A count would make subjectivism the standard, because agreement does not decide what is real.

exercises.prompt: An engineer checks the loads, integrates them with the known strength of the steel, and states whether the beam will hold. What made the statement knowledge?

choices.text: Reason identifying and integrating the sensory evidence
A revelation that arrived before the loads were measured
The crew's hope that the beam would hold
The fact that the statement was useful, whether or not it matched the steel

feedback.note: Knowledge here is reason's identification of the evidence. The senses supplied the material, and reason integrated it. A revelation or a hope would bypass that work, which is mysticism, because neither is a means of knowledge. Usefulness does not make a mismatched statement true. Truth is the recognition of what the beam is.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed standard to the view it expresses.

pairs.right: The only means of knowledge and the only standard of truth
Mysticism: a non-sensory claim to knowledge
Pragmatism: success substituted for recognition of reality
Subjectivism: agreement treated as the author of truth

feedback.note: Reason is the only standard because truth is the recognition of reality, and reason is the only means of that recognition. Feeling bypasses the evidence. What works changes the standard without identifying the facts. A vote treats truth as subjectivism, a product of preference rather than of evidence integrated by reason.

exercises.prompt: Complete the statement of the only standard of truth.

parts.text: Reason, man's only means of knowledge, is his only standard of

feedback.quote: Truth is the recognition of reality; reason, man's only means of knowledge, is his only standard of truth.
feedback.citation: Ayn Rand, Galt's Speech, For the New Intellectual, 126
feedback.note: The standard of truth is reason, because truth is the recognition of reality and reason is the only means of knowledge. Feeling, utility, and consensus are rival standards. They fail because none of them identifies and integrates the sensory evidence. They offer mysticism, pragmatism, or subjectivism in its place.

exercises.prompt: Someone "reasons" from a revelation and calls the result knowledge because the inferences are tidy. What is missing?

choices.text: A stronger feeling, which would turn the revelation into evidence
A base in sensory evidence. Tidiness from a revelation is not reason
A vote to confirm the revelation, which would make it reason
Nothing. Any tidy inference is reason, whatever the starting point

feedback.note: Reason identifies and integrates the material the senses provide. A revelation is not that material. Inferences from it can be verbally tidy and still be detached from the only source of information. The error dresses mysticism in the vocabulary of reason, because the means has already bypassed sensory evidence.

exercises.prompt: A true identification also helps the engineer build. Why does that not make usefulness the standard of truth?

choices.text: It does. A helpful error is true by the only standard, so usefulness can overrule the beam
It does. Reason is simply the name for what happens to work, success replacing the identification
Usefulness is a consequence of recognizing reality, not the test that makes the recognition true
It does not, because a true identification must be useless, help to the builder making it false

feedback.note: A true identification is what one has to act on, so it is useful to a living person. That consequence does not replace the standard. Truth remains the recognition of reality by reason. The error is pragmatism, because "it helps" does not decide what the beam is. The evidence and the identification do.

exercises.prompt: Build the double claim about reason, knowledge, and truth.

feedback.note: Reason is the only means of knowledge and the only standard of truth. An optional means would leave room for faith or feeling, which is mysticism, because those bypass sensory evidence. Feeling is not a standard of truth. Truth is the recognition of reality, and only reason performs that recognition.

exercises.prompt: What does mysticism claim as a means of knowledge?

choices.text: Reason, identifying and integrating what the senses provide, later renamed faith
The admission that knowledge is impossible, revelation being only a softer denial
A method of non-contradictory identification of the facts, carried out by consulting a feeling
A means that bypasses sensory evidence, such as faith, revelation, or feeling used as proof

feedback.note: Mysticism claims a means of knowledge that bypasses sensory evidence. Faith, revelation, and feeling used as proof are forms of that claim. Reason does the opposite: it integrates the evidence. Skepticism is a different rival, because it denies that knowledge is possible rather than offering a non-sensory route to it.

exercises.prompt: An engineer feels afraid of a bridge and treats the fear itself as proof that the bridge will fail. What is the error?

choices.text: He used a feeling as proof, which is mysticism
He used fear as a signal to go and check the evidence
He identified the loads and integrated them with the strength of the steel
He concluded that knowledge of bridges is impossible

feedback.note: The fear reports his estimate, not the condition of the bridge. Using it as proof bypasses sensory evidence. That is mysticism. Checking the bridge because he feels uneasy would be different, because the feeling would be a motive to look, not the evidence. Denying that bridges can be known would be skepticism, not this error.

exercises.prompt: A message is offered as revelation, and the hearer is told not to check it against observation. Why is that mysticism rather than reason?

choices.text: Because the message was printed, and print is a percept
Because the claim to knowledge bypasses sensory evidence on principle
Because any unwelcome message is mystical by definition
Because reason forbids looking whenever a conclusion is important

feedback.note: The mystical move is the instruction not to check the message against observation. Knowledge is being claimed by a route that bypasses the only source of information. Print can be perceived, but the content is not being offered as a conclusion from evidence. It is offered as revelation, which is mysticism, because the ban on checking is the method.

exercises.prompt: Match each episode to the cognitive claim it makes.

pairs.left: Fear offered as proof the bridge will fail
pairs.right: Mysticism: feeling used as a means of knowledge

pairs.left: Fear used as a reason to inspect the bridge
pairs.right: Not mysticism. The evidence is still to be looked at
Mysticism: a claimed means that bypasses sensory evidence

pairs.left: Loads integrated with the known strength of the steel
pairs.right: Reason, the only means of knowledge

feedback.note: Mysticism is a claim to know by faith, revelation, or feeling used as proof. An emotion that sends someone to look is not yet that claim, because the evidence remains the standard. Sealing a message against observation is the bypass. Integrating the loads is reason, which does not claim a route around the senses.

exercises.prompt: Complete the description of the means mysticism claims.

parts.text: Mysticism claims a means of knowledge that bypasses sensory

feedback.note: Mysticism bypasses sensory evidence and offers faith, revelation, or feeling as proof instead. It does not bypass error, grammar, or courtesy. Those are not the source of information. The error is the claim to a second means of knowledge, because reason working on the evidence of the senses is the only means there is.

exercises.prompt: Someone says mysticism is simply the view that knowledge is impossible. What has he confused it with?

choices.text: Reason. Mysticism is the name for integrating sensory evidence, faith as integration
Nothing. Faith is the admission that no means of knowledge exists, faith as refusal
Skepticism. Mysticism claims a non-sensory means. It does not merely deny knowledge
Pragmatism. Mysticism means truth is whatever works, success replacing identification

feedback.note: Mysticism and skepticism are different denials of reason. Mysticism claims to know by a means that bypasses sensory evidence. Skepticism says knowledge cannot be had. Calling faith a confession of ignorance misses the claim faith actually makes, because the mystic offers a positive route, not a blank refusal of every conclusion.

exercises.prompt: A chemist trusts a method because it has repeatedly matched careful observation. A colleague calls that trust faith. What is wrong with the charge?

choices.text: Trust based on evidence is mysticism, and the charge is correct, observation counting as faith
Any confidence about a method bypasses the senses, checked records counting as revelation
Observation cannot support a method, so the trust must be revelation, a match treated as a bypass
The trust rests on sensory evidence. Mystical faith is a claimed means that bypasses evidence

feedback.note: Confidence earned by repeated observation is a conclusion of reason, not a bypass of the senses. Mystical faith claims knowledge apart from that evidence, or against the duty to check. The charge confuses a word, because it treats every reliance as mysticism. Reliance on integrated evidence is the opposite of mysticism.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim that names mysticism by the means it offers.

feedback.note: Mysticism claims a means that bypasses sensory evidence, whether the offered means is faith, revelation, or feeling used as proof. Integrating that evidence would be reason. A bare denial that knowledge is possible would be skepticism. The mystical error is the positive claim to a route around the only source of information, because no such route exists.

exercises.prompt: What does skepticism say about knowledge?

choices.text: Knowledge is not possible, so reason does not succeed
Knowledge is possible by faith, revelation, or feeling
Knowledge is the recognition of reality by reason
Knowledge is possible only of things as they are in themselves, by the mind's forms

feedback.note: Skepticism denies that knowledge is possible, and so denies that reason succeeds. Mysticism is a different claim: it offers a non-sensory means. Reason holds that knowledge is the recognition of reality. The parenthetical about forms does not describe a defense of knowledge of things as they are, because if the forms constitute phenomena, things as they are stay unknowable.

exercises.prompt: If the mind's forms constitute the objects of experience, what follows about things as they are?

choices.text: They are known directly, because the forms copy things as they are. Direct acquaintance is claimed.
They stay unknowable. That is a skeptical result, not a claim that appearances are random fakes.
They are reached by faith, which bypasses the forms. Faith reaches past the forms anyway.
They change when a vote adopts a new set of forms. A vote changes what the forms hide.

feedback.note: If phenomena are constituted by the mind's forms, things as they are in themselves remain unknowable. That is a skeptical result. It is not the cartoon in which the senses spray arbitrary pictures and appearances are nothing. Faith would turn the issue into mysticism. A vote would turn it into subjectivism, because neither is the consequence of the forms.

exercises.prompt: Which summary cartoons the view that things in themselves stay unknowable?

choices.text: The mind's forms structure experience, so things as they are are not known
Reason identifies and integrates the material the senses provide
The senses spray random pictures, so the world one sees is nothing at all
An error of identification is a mistake in thinking about real evidence

feedback.note: The position at issue says the mind's forms constitute phenomena, so the noumenal thing stays unknowable. That is skepticism about things as they are. The random-pictures summary is a cartoon, because it replaces that thesis with the claim that appearances are nothing. A misidentification is a different and lesser error. It does not make the evidence a fake.

exercises.prompt: Match each claim to the answer it gives about knowledge.

pairs.left: Things as they are stay unknowable if the mind constitutes phenomena
pairs.right: A skeptical result, stated without a cartoon

pairs.left: The senses spray random pictures and appearances are nothing
pairs.right: A cartoon, not the thesis about forms and things in themselves

pairs.left: Faith reaches things as they are
pairs.right: Mysticism, a claimed means around the evidence

pairs.left: Reason knows reality by integrating sensory evidence
pairs.right: The rejection of the skeptical result

feedback.note: The noumenal outcome is skeptical: if the mind's forms constitute phenomena, things as they are stay unknowable. The spray-of-pictures line cartoons that view, because it denies even the appearances the thesis still talks about. Faith is mysticism, not this argument. Reason rejects the result by treating the senses as contact with reality.

exercises.prompt: Complete the skeptical conclusion about things as they are.

parts.text: If the mind constitutes phenomena, things as they are stay

feedback.note: The skeptical result is that things as they are stay unknowable. Calling them obvious would deny the noumenal gap rather than state it. Calling them optional or voted would be subjectivism, because the thesis is not that people may choose whether things have an identity. It is that identity, so understood, cannot be known.

exercises.prompt: Because people sometimes misidentify what they see, someone concludes that knowledge is impossible. What is the mistake?

choices.text: One error proves the senses invent their objects and that faith must replace them
Knowledge is impossible only of percepts, and concepts are infallible
A misidentification is a contradiction in reality, so reality cannot be known
An error presupposes a standard. It does not show that knowledge cannot succeed

feedback.note: A misidentification is a failure measured against the possibility of getting the identification right. Generalizing from some errors to the impossibility of knowledge is skepticism. It does not follow, because the standard used to call the conclusion an error is itself a piece of knowledge. Replacing the percept with faith would add mysticism on top.

exercises.prompt: Which remark is a contextual limit on knowledge, rather than skepticism?

choices.text: I do not yet know what is in the locked drawer. I do know the lamp is on
No one can know anything, including the contents of this room
Things as they are are unknowable because the mind manufactures phenomena
Every claim is equally baseless, including the claim that the lamp is on

feedback.note: A contextual limit names something outside the evidence one has, and it leaves standing what the evidence does support. Skepticism denies that knowledge is possible at all. The locked drawer is unknown so far. The lamp is not therefore unknown. Treating every gap as the ruin of every conclusion confuses a limit with skepticism, because a gap is not a proof that reason fails.

exercises.prompt: Build the statement of what skepticism denies.

feedback.note: Skepticism denies that knowledge is possible, and so denies that reason succeeds. Shifting the denial onto faith would describe a quarrel inside mysticism, not this position. Faith used as proof is a claimed means of knowledge, which skepticism does not offer. The skeptical claim is that there is no successful means.

exercises.prompt: If reason is rejected, what kind of action is one left with?

choices.text: A second, equally valid means of knowing the facts
Action with no regard for the facts, or action against the facts
Automatic caution that keeps every action matched to the evidence
A new standard on which truth is whatever works
